output.brief: The Android drop is not caused by release 6.14, the Android security patch, or bots. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane auto-updated the edge rule pack. A new rule, AUTO-LIB-17, blocks password-login requests that come from the nettle-http library without an edge session cookie. It returns HTTP 403. The first block was at 10:41. The drop appears at 10:41 on every app version and OS version, and in both patched and unpatched phones. Quick-unlock is unaffected. About 41,300 real installs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. Users retry, which is why password attempts rose. Rollback of 6.14 would not help. The 18% rise in calls is probably partly due to the fee notices, so I would not attribute it all to this. I'm about 90% sure of the cause. Next steps: ask Corvane to set that rule to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping all other protections active. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Don't raise bot sensitivity. Don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Ask Corvane to test new rules against the bank's traffic before applying them.
